---
title: "Debugging"
engine: markdown
---

## Verbose Mode

Enable verbose output to see what quarto-term is doing during execution:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    verbose: true
```

This prints to stderr:

- Session startup (shell, prompt)
- Each line being sent (prefixed with `>`)
- Errors and timeouts
- Recording paths

## Terminal Recordings

Record sessions to asciicast or termshow format for playback:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    record: "session.cast"
```

Supported formats (detected by file extension):

- `.cast` --- asciicast v2, playable with [asciinema](https://asciinema.org/)
- `.termshow` --- works with [termshow](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-docs/)

Record to multiple files simultaneously:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    record:
      - "session.cast"
      - "session.termshow"
```

## Assertions

Validate terminal output with the `assert` option. Use it at the line level to check a specific command's output:

````markdown
```{term}
echo "hello world" #! assert: "hello world"
python3 -c "print(2+2)" #! assert: "4"
```
````

Or at the cell level to check the entire cell output:

````markdown
```{term}
#| assert: "hello"
echo "hello world"
```
````

Multiple patterns (all must match):

````markdown
```{term}
#| assert: ["hello", "world"]
echo "hello world"
```
````

The pattern is tried as a regex first, falling back to a substring match if it's not valid regex.

## `quarto-term check`

Run assertions as a CI-friendly check:

```bash
quarto-term check docs/tutorial.qmd
```

This runs `quarto render` under the hood and fails (exit code 1) if any assertion doesn't match. Use it in CI to catch documentation drift:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/check.yml
- name: Check terminal examples
  run: quarto-term check docs/tutorial.qmd
```

### Recording during check

Combine assertion checking with terminal recording:

```bash
quarto-term check --record session.cast docs/tutorial.qmd
```

This validates all assertions AND produces a recording file in one pass.

## Caching

quarto-term caches execution results to speed up repeated renders. If no cell inputs or configuration have changed, the binary is skipped entirely:

```
quarto-term: cache hit (a3f2b1c4)
```

The cache is stored in `.quarto-term-cache/` (add to `.gitignore`), one entry per document. Results that contain a cell error are not cached, so failing cells run again on the next render.

The cache key covers:

- all cells of the document and the quarto-term configuration;
- the quarto-term version and the binary itself;
- in Docker mode, the local image's id, so a new image behind the same tag (e.g. `:latest`) re-runs the document. With `pull: always`, the image is pulled before the key is computed;
- the contents of host files sourced through `init`;
- the contents of the files and directories listed in `cache-depends`.

It does **not** cover the contents of mounted volumes or anything fetched from the network. If cells depend on files that aren't in the document, such as scripts in a mounted directory that `init` sources inside the container, list them in `cache-depends` (paths are relative to the working directory; directories are hashed recursively):

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    init: "source /setup/setup.zsh"
    cache-depends:
      - setup              # mounted at /setup
    docker:
      image: "myorg/toolbox:latest"
      volumes:
        - "./setup:/setup:ro"
```

Hashing is cheap for scripts, but avoid listing large data directories. Run with `verbose: true` to see the key and what went into it:

```
quarto-term: cache key 5d41402a (engine 7c4a8d09, image 1aeded7acb69, 3 dependency files)
```

To force re-execution:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    cache: false
```

Or simply delete the `.quarto-term-cache/` directory.

## Using a specific binary

By default, quarto-term uses the binary downloaded into `_extensions/term/bin/`, falling back to a local `target/release` or `target/debug` build. To use a specific binary instead, for example while developing quarto-term itself, set `QUARTO_TERM_BINARY`:

```bash
QUARTO_TERM_BINARY=./target/debug/quarto-term quarto render
```

## Common Issues

### Timeout errors

If a cell times out, the shell likely didn't return to the prompt. Common causes:

- The command is interactive (waiting for input)
- The prompt regex doesn't match the actual prompt
- The shell sends terminal queries that aren't answered

Increase the timeout or check your prompt configuration:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    timeout: 30
```

### PS2 (continuation prompt) issues

Multi-line commands can hang if the continuation prompt isn't detected. Configure `ps2` or `ps2-regex`:

```yaml
extensions:
  term:
    ps2: ">"
```
